processing: Orthodox Darjeeling tea from a bio-organic estate, mostly black, with green and white lots as well; first flush is lightly oxidised, as usual in Darjeeling.
harvest_season: First flush in spring is the main draw, and its bushes were replanted with that picking in mind.
appearance_dry: As with other Darjeeling first flushes, a mix of olive-green and brown leaf with pale tips.
appearance_liquor: A pale golden amber, typical of Darjeeling first flush.
appearance_wet: Typically greenish leaf with coppery edges, as with other first flushes.
taste_profile: Few independent tasting notes are available; as with other Darjeeling first flushes, expect a delicate, floral and lightly brisk cup.

brewing.notes: General first flush guidance: water a little off the boil and no milk.

vintage_note: Sold by harvest year and flush, usually first flush, with the grade on the label. It is often sold as organic, so look for current certification. First flush is best within a year or so of picking.
description:
Tukdah is an organic Darjeeling garden in the Teesta Valley, covering 557 hectares with 288 under tea, between 2,500 and 6,500 feet. The nearby settlement is usually spelled Takdah, while the tea trade writes Tukdah.

It is first flush that made the name. The estate also makes green and white teas, and its output is put at about 210,000 kg a year.

Expect the delicate, floral profile usual for Darjeeling's spring picking rather than the muscatel of a second flush. Use water a little off the boil and keep an eye on the time, since long steeps bring out astringency.

The label should tell you the year, flush and grade. Comparing one spring against the next is a good way to learn the garden.
history:
Tukdah is dated to 1864. In the 1960s the original bushes were uprooted and replanted with the aim of producing a delicate first flush, which explains its present focus.

It passed from Darjeeling Consolidated Ltd to Darjeeling Plantation Industries Ltd, and has been with the Chamong Group since 2004. These details rest mainly on a single regional guide.
